Intuit Inc. 650-944-3663 650-944-3036 kendra_goodenough@intuit.com kali_fry@intuit.com Intuit Reports First-Quarter Results and Enters Agreement to Sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons Global Business Solutions Online Ecosystem Revenue Grew 20 percent; Consumer Revenue Grew 7 percent MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. - November 19, 2026 - Intuit Inc. (Nasdaq: INTU), the global financial technology platform that makes TurboTax , Credit Karma , QuickBooks , Mailchimp , Intuit Enterprise Suite , and Intuit Accountant Suite , announced financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended October 31, announced guidance for the second-quarter of fiscal 2027 and updated guidance for the full-year. Intuit also announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons. "We delivered a solid first quarter, with results above the top end of our guidance," said Sasan Goodarzi, Intuit's chairman and chief executive officer. "Our AI-driven expert platform increasingly does more of the work for consumers, businesses and accountants, turning financial data into intelligence and action that helps them achieve better outcomes. I'm pleased with the innovation we've launched this quarter, and we're focused on disciplined execution as we build durable, long-term growth." Financial Highlights For the first quarter: • Total revenue increased 12 percent to $4.4 billion. • Global Business Solutions revenue increased 15 percent to $3.1 billion. • Consumer revenue increased 7 percent to $958 million. • Mailchimp revenue decreased 1 percent to $313 million. • GAAP operating income increased 63 percent to $868 million. • Non-GAAP operating income increased 46 percent to $1.0 billion. • GAAP diluted earnings per share increased 63 percent to $2.59. 1 • Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share increased 56 percent to $2.91. Unless otherwise noted, all growth rates refer to the current period versus the comparable prior-year period, and the business metrics and associated growth rates refer to worldwide business metrics. "Our first quarter results demonstrate progress against our strategy and reflect disciplined execution," said Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's chief financial officer. "We remain focused on building the foundation for durable long-term revenue growth while expanding margins and increasing capital returns to shareholders."
